content.title: About
content.content: Sushi with egg is a traditional Japanese dish consisting of vinegared rice wrapped in nori and topped with a thin layer of tamago (Japanese omelette). The egg adds a delicate flavor, slight sweetness, and extra protein.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tamago is often seasoned with soy sauce, sugar, and mirin, giving it a characteristic golden hue.
Egg sushi is commonly served as a cucumber roll (kappa maki) with cucumber inside as well.
In Japan, egg symbolizes prosperity and is frequently served during celebrations.
Tamago sushi is often used as a filler between more expensive ingredients in sushi bars.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs provide a complete source of high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Tamago supplies vitamin B12, riboflavin, and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Eggs contain iron, phosphorus, and selenium, important for blood health and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Egg sushi fits moderate low‑carb diets, as the main carb source is rice while the egg adds minimal sugar.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin in the yolk help maintain healthy vision.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg proteins.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Egg yolk contains cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should monitor portion size.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Improperly cooked egg can carry a risk of salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Egg sushi is usually eaten with chopsticks, sometimes lightly dipped in soy sauce. It pairs well with pickled ginger, wasabi, and marinated ginger.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store prepared sushi in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for no more than 24 hours. For longer storage, keep the rice and egg separate to prevent the nori from becoming soggy.
